title: fix(app-shell): under a wall the security catalog's pages are read-only for a tenant and say why; the operator keeps write (objectui#12183)
body:
Fixes #12183

Clause-②: no

Part of #7611: this is its C9 remainder. The epic stays open with its seat.

## What changed

Under a tenancy wall (`isolated` or `group`), the security catalog is the platform operator's (objectstack ADR-0131 D3). Since objectstack#22895 (`06cc45dc3`), every door that writes a position, permission set or capability refuses anyone else, `manage_metadata` included. The console still offered a walled tenant holding `manage_metadata` Save, New, Clone, the active switch and the History rollback. Each of those answered 403.

- **One predicate.** `walledCatalogReadOnly` (with `useWalledCatalogReadOnly`) in `views/metadata-admin/catalog-scope.ts`. It is true for a catalog type, under a wall, for a caller without operator standing. It reads only what the server publishes: the posture (`features.tenancyPosture`, through `useTenancyPosture` and `postureHasOrgWall`) and the session's `user.isPlatformAdmin` (read `=== true`). Every catalog write affordance reads this predicate, so no two surfaces can disagree.
- **It extends the existing caller tier; it adds no second gate.** `canAuthor` becomes `canAuthor && !walled` wherever a write is offered: `ResourceListPage` (New, `CatalogActiveCell`'s switch), `ResourceEditPage` (`canWrite`, the artifact-locked banner's New, the create form, the History sheet's rollback), and `PermissionMatrixEditor` (`writable`, `lockedByArtifactTier`, which offers Clone).
- **The reason is the server rule, not a missing permission.** Each surface names the wall where the wall decides, meaning where the item tier would otherwise admit the write. The list shows its existing `catalog-readonly-reason` line. The generic editor shows a new `walled-catalog-readonly-banner`. The matrix shows a `perm-walled-readonly` note, and its identity badge reads `perm.readOnly.walled`. The capability notice and the type notice step aside there. A stock capability, which no one can write, still names its type tier.
- **Assignment is untouched.** `PositionHoldersSection` and `AssignedUsersSection` gate only on `busy` and the adapter, and both are pinned writable under the wall.
- **Rider** (objectui#7611 pointer 6117177535). The designer auto-on effect in `ResourceEditPage` reads `canWrite` instead of `itemWritable`. `useCanAuthorMetadata` is hoisted next to the item tier, so a caller without `manage_metadata` no longer lands in design mode with no Save.
- The `@object-ui/app-shell` README's "The Setup catalog" gates bullet describes the wall. The changeset is `.changeset/12183-walled-catalog-readonly.md` (`@object-ui/app-shell` patch).

No spec field, no `@object-ui/i18n` pack key, and no published export, prop or type member. The predicate is module-local: the package entry re-exports only `ENVIRONMENT_SCOPE_QUERY` from `catalog-scope.ts`.

## Measured first

### H1: the posture
On `main` at `5b20aed`, `ResourceListPage` read `useTenancyPosture` for one thing only: to choose `engine.catalog.readOnly.walled` over `.single` as the reason line of a caller without `manage_metadata`. No write affordance read the posture. `ResourceEditPage` and `PermissionMatrixEditor` did not read it at all. The new gate therefore folds into the existing `canAuthor` caller tier.

### H2: the operator standing (the deciding hypothesis): served, so read it
This was read on objectstack `origin/main` at `1bd612bd6`. `git merge-base --is-ancestor 06cc45dc3 origin/main` exits 0, and a positive answer from `--is-ancestor` needs no control leg.
- **The exemption predicate** is `walledCatalogWriteVerdict` in `@objectstack/metadata-core`, file `meta-write-capability.ts`. It admits `isSystem`, or `callerPosture === PLATFORM_OPERATOR_POSTURE`, which is `'PLATFORM_ADMIN'`. Every door passes the execution context's `posture`: `RestServer.walledCatalogRefusal`, the dispatcher's `PUT` in `runtime/src/domains/meta.ts`, `createWalledCatalogDataDoorRefusal`, and the clone door. The activation gate reads `ec.posture === 'PLATFORM_ADMIN'` itself.
- **Where the rung comes from.** `resolveAuthzContext` sets `ctx.posture = grants.posture`, where `grants` comes from `resolveUserAuthzGrants` scoped to the request's organization. `derivePosture` returns `PLATFORM_ADMIN` only from the unscoped `admin_full_access` grant or the declared-administrator email anchor.
- **The served fact.** plugin-auth `auth-manager.ts` `customSession` builds the session payload's `user.isPlatformAdmin` as `grants.posture === 'PLATFORM_ADMIN'`. It uses the same `resolveUserAuthzGrants`, scoped to `session.activeOrganizationId`. The comment there says it is "byte-for-byte what `hasPlatformAdminStanding` returns". The merged dogfood pin `wall-catalog-refusal.dogfood.test.ts` ("guard the guard") asserts that the walled tenant's `session.user.isPlatformAdmin` is `false`.
- The console already reads this flag as the rung (`useWorkspaceAdminStatus`, leg 3a). ⛔ It never reads `positions.includes('platform_admin')`, because a tenant can write that name.

### H3: the surfaces at environment scope, and what this PR does to each

| Surface | File · symbol | Gate on `main` | Walled tenant holding `manage_metadata`, on `main` | After |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| List · New | `ResourceListPage` · `canCreate` | type tier, and `canAuthor` in env scope | offered | withheld; reason line shown |
| List · active switch | `ResourceListPage` · `CatalogActiveCell` `canSwitch` | `canAuthor` | live | disabled; states the state |
| List · reason line | `ResourceListPage` · `catalog-readonly-reason` | only when not `canAuthor` | absent | the walled sentence |
| List · type actions | `MetadataTypeActions` (list toolbar) | server-declared | none declared for these types | unchanged |
| Position or capability editor · Edit, Save, autosave, Publish, Discard draft, Reset/Delete | `ResourceEditPage` · `canWrite` | `itemWritable && canAuthor` | offered on a position; a stock capability is closed by its type | withheld; `walled-catalog-readonly-banner` |
| Editor · design mode auto-on | `ResourceEditPage` effect | `itemWritable` | n/a (the catalog types have no designer) | reads `canWrite` (rider) |
| Editor · artifact-locked banner's New | `ResourceEditPage` · `showArtifactLockedBanner` | `canAuthor` | offered | withheld |
| Editor · History sheet rollback | `ResourceEditPage` · `HistoryPanel` `onRollback` | none | offered | offered on `canWrite` only |
| Editor · create page Save | `ResourceEditPage` (create mode) | `canWrite` | offered | withheld; form read-only; banner |
| Permission-set editor · Save, autosave, grants | `PermissionMatrixEditor` · `writable` | type, host and `canAuthor` | offered | withheld; `perm-walled-readonly` |
| Permission-set editor · Clone to customize | `PermissionMatrixEditor` · `lockedByArtifactTier` | includes `canAuthor` | offered on a packaged set | withheld |
| Permission-set editor · identity badge | `PermissionMatrixEditor` | host, artifact or type | named the TYPE ("no runtime write channel"), which is false here | `perm.readOnly.walled` |
| Position holders · Add, Remove | `PositionHoldersSection` | `busy`, adapter | writable | writable (pinned) |
| Permission-set holders · Add, Remove | `AssignedUsersSection` | `busy` | writable | writable (pinned) |
| Standalone history route · rollback | `ResourceHistoryPage` · `HistoryPanel` | none | offered | **unchanged**: outside the claimed file surface (see Acceptance notes) |

The console-side measurement is the new pin file run against the untouched `main` sources. It gave 17 failed and 10 passed. Every walled-tenant case was offered the write. Every control passed, once a harness slip was fixed: a writable form-only editor draws Edit twice.

### H4: what the server answers, per surface (**code-read** of the doors plus the merged dogfood pins; no live boot of my own)

| Door (surface) | Walled tenant | Operator | Source |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| `PUT /meta/:type/:name` (New, Save, create) | 403 `FORBIDDEN` on REST; 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` on the dispatcher | admitted | `walledCatalogRefusal`, dispatcher `PUT` · dogfood "org A cannot create a position, a permission set or a capability at `/meta`" and "CONTROL: the platform operator still saves the catalog" (200) |
| `DELETE /meta/:type/:name` (Reset/Delete) | 403 `FORBIDDEN` | admitted | dogfood "…nor delete one" · operator by code-read |
| publish, rollback doors | 403 | admitted | code-read: REST asks `metaWriteCapabilityVerdict` and then `walledCatalogRefusal` on both |
| `POST /security/_activation/:type/:name` (switch) | 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` | admitted | `activation-gate.ts`, `ACTIVATION_DENY_STATUS` · the W-stage PR's own pre-change table: 403 |
| `POST /security/permission-sets/:name/clone` (Clone) | 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` | 200 | dogfood "the clone door refuses org A…" and "CONTROL: the platform operator still clones…" |
| `POST /data/sys_user_permission_set` (assign a set) | 201 | admitted | dogfood "CONTROL: org A still assigns…" |
| `sys_user_position` rows (assign a position) | not judged | admitted | code-read: `WALLED_CATALOG_OBJECT_TYPES` names only `sys_position`, `sys_permission_set` and `sys_capability` |
| `single`, a `manage_metadata` holder, `PUT /meta/position` | 200 | 200 | dogfood "single: … saves a position: 200" |

Why there is no live boot: it would need a separate objectstack checkout on `main`, built, and booted walled, with an organization-scoped `manage_metadata` grant seeded in-process. That is the harness the merged `wall-catalog-refusal.dogfood.test.ts` already runs against exactly these doors. Every row above says which source it rests on.

### H5: the copy
The sentence already existed. `engine.catalog.readOnly.walled` (objectui#12089, en and zh) says "the platform operator defines {type} items for every organization in Studio; your organization assigns them". That is a server rule, distinct from `engine.edit.capabilityReadOnly`. It is reused on all three pages. The one new key is the matrix badge's short label, `perm.readOnly.walled` (en and zh), in the designer table `views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts`. It sits beside the three existing badge labels, and its tooltip is the walled sentence.

## Deviations from the suggested route
1. **The gate does not read the environment scope.** The server's verdict has no scope input. The REST `PUT /meta` door asks `walledCatalogRefusal` before it reads `?package=` or `mode=draft`, so Studio's package-door drafts of a catalog item are refused the same way. Keying on the scope would also contradict `catalog-scope.ts`'s own header ("a VIEW scope, never an authority"). Studio's list and editors for these three types therefore also go read-only for a walled tenant. A pin covers the list and the matrix there.
2. **The editor's History sheet rollback** now reads Save's gate (`canWrite`). The REST rollback door asks the same capability and walled verdicts. This also withholds rollback from a non-walled caller who cannot save, which the door refuses as well.
3. **The README** (`packages/app-shell/README.md`) is outside the claimed file surface. It is edited because objectui AGENTS.md #2 requires the package README to describe the gate it documents.

## Tests (HEAD `3bdffbd`; the code is unchanged since `eed4f3e`)
- New pin file `views/metadata-admin/walledCatalogReadOnly-12183.test.tsx`, 28 tests. It covers the predicate's posture × type × rung table. For every catalog type it checks that the walled tenant is read-only on the list (`isolated` and `group` × permission and position), the position editor, the create page, a hatch-elevated capability, and the matrix: no Save, no Clone, the Studio package door locked, no History rollback. Controls: the operator under the same wall is writable everywhere; `single` and an unknown posture are unchanged; a non-catalog type keeps New; a stock capability names its type tier. Assignment stays writable: the real sections are rendered, and Add writes `sys_user_position` and `sys_user_permission_set` by name. The rider is pinned in one case, with a control.
- **Ablations** use `ablation-replace.mjs` from the committed state. Each mutation was proven on disk, then restored to the HEAD blob with `git diff HEAD` empty. The subject resolves from `src`, through a relative import and the vitest alias, so no `dist` was involved.

| Leg | Mutation | Red | Green |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| F | the predicate returns false | 14 (predicate unit and every walled pin) | 13 (every control, both assignment pins, the rider) |
| A | the list ignores the wall | 6 (list pins) | 21 |
| B | the editor ignores the wall | 4 (editor pins) | 23 |
| C | the matrix ignores the wall | 3 (matrix pins) | 24 |
| D | the auto-on effect reads `itemWritable` | 1 (rider) | 26 |
| E1 | position holders hidden unless `canWrite` (over-gate) | 1 (assignment) | 26 |
| E2 | permission-set holders hidden unless `writable` | 1 (assignment) | 26 |
| G | History rollback ungated | 1 (rollback) | 27 |

  The first try at leg F was refused by the tool before anything ran, because the replacement re-contained the anchor. It was re-anchored and rerun.
- **Union at `eed4f3e`:** every test file naming a touched module, plus the 12141 and 12169 pins, the holder sections and the posture parity test. That is 104 files and 946 tests, all passing. The three tests that read the app-shell README passed at `3bdffbd` (58 tests).
- **Gates:** `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...'` (28 tasks); `type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`; the test project compiles the new pin, confirmed by `--listFilesOnly`); `check:i18n-designer-parity`, `check:i18n-drift` and `check:i18n-keys`; changeset presence, no-major, claims and pending literals; `check:control-bytes`; `check:new-line-citations` (0 new); `check-vi-mock-override-shape`, `-inherit` and `-specifiers`; `check-test-path-roots`; the doc gates (links, fences, JSON fences, expression carriage). All exit 0. Targeted eslint on the six touched source files, run the way CI's per-package `eslint .` runs it, gives 0 errors, and per-file warning counts equal to `main`. The config is not type-aware and no repo rule reads other files from disk, so this narrowing moves no untouched file's verdict. `check-readme-exports` is NOT MEASURED: no package's `dist` type entry is built here, which is a prerequisite and not a verdict, and the README diff adds no fenced block or import.

## Acceptance notes
- **The standalone history route** (`ResourceHistoryPage`) still passes `onRollback` to every caller. It is reached from the permission-set editor's History button and by URL. The rollback door refuses a walled tenant, and any caller without `manage_metadata`. It is outside this card's file surface. The fix has the same shape: read the item and caller gates there.
- **The header writability badge** (`PageShell`'s `WritabilityBadge`) is a TYPE badge. It still reads "writable" for a walled tenant, exactly as it already did for a caller without `manage_metadata`. Changing it would change `MetadataPageShell`'s props, which this card rules out.
- **The matrix badge for a non-walled caller without `manage_metadata`** still names the type tier ("no runtime write channel"). That label is false for `permission`, and it predates this PR.
- **The catalog type list** is restated in `catalog-scope.ts`. The server's `SECURITY_CATALOG_TYPES` lives in `@objectstack/metadata-core`, which this repo does not depend on, and the spec exports none. Nothing re-derives the two. A fourth type added upstream would be a refusal this list does not announce, shown as sent.
- **The posture seam.** plugin-auth's public config falls back to the requested posture when no `tenancy` service is registered, while the doors read that absence as inert. On such a deployment the console would show read-only where the server admits. That is the conservative direction, and it was not measured.
- **Timing.** The posture arrives through the auth config's cached promise. If it resolved after the item load, the designer could already be in design mode. Catalog types have no designer, and the console's top bar reads the same promise first, so this was not observed.
